question: For real x,y, consider L1: 3(x - 2y) + 4 = 2x - y + 9 and L2: -2x + 10y = -10. Graph both equations and label L1 and L2, even if they share the same geometric line. Mark P = (0,-1), Q = (5,0), R = (0,0), and identify which solve BOTH equations. State the full solution set and whether the system determines a unique x-coordinate.

qualitativeClaims.expected: L1 simplifies to x−5y=5. Dividing L2 by −2 gives x−5y=5.
P=(0,−1) and Q=(5,0) lie on both lines; R=(0,0) lies on neither.
No. As t ranges over ℝ, x=5+5t takes infinitely many values.
